note: CLN3 mutations cause both classic syndromic juvenile Batten disease (JNCL) with dementia, seizures, and neurodegeneration, and isolated/nonsyndromic retinal degeneration (RP101) lacking systemic neurological decline.

evidence.text: Biallelic variants in CLN3 lead to a spectrum ranging from severe neurodegeneration with retinal involvement (JNCL) to retina-restricted conditions where patients present with nonsyndromic inherited retinal disease.

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: Biallelic variants in CLN3 lead to a spectrum of diseases, ranging from severe neurodegeneration with retinal involvement (juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis) to retina-restricted conditions.

numbers.metric: nonsyndromic IRD patients with biallelic CLN3 variants

evidence.text: Mutations in CLN3 associated with late-onset, non-syndromic retinal dystrophy did not develop neurological symptoms over prolonged follow-up, contrasting with classic juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis.

source.title: Clinical and molecular characterization of non-syndromic retinal dystrophy due to c.175G>A mutation in ceroid lipofuscinosis neuronal 3 (CLN3)
source.quote: Mutation of the CLN3 gene, associated with juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, has recently been associated with late-onset, non-syndromic retinal dystrophy.
